ca_tenacious_d_wall.blurb: A small wall in the southern end of the Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine, in the Eastern Sierra, sitting around 4,650 feet. Ten routes split between trad and bolted sport lines, and the grades cluster around the 5.10 range, with a couple of easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range and a single 5.11. Pitches are short, roughly 45 to 75 feet, with lowering or rappel anchors up top. A few of the lines cross one another, so it pays to read route descriptions before pulling on. It works well as a quick stop for a climber already cragging in the neighbouring Gunga Din zone, and it is a reasonable option for a leader stepping up to 5.10.

ca_tropics_wall.blurb: One of the more remote walls in the Land of the Lost cluster on Horse Mountain, inland from Arcata and Eureka in far northwest California. Roughly ten routes, mostly short bolted sport lines of four or five clips, plus a pair of trad lines and a top-rope. The grades lean hard: a few 5.10s, a good batch of 5.11s, two at 5.12, and one easier warm-up near 5.8. The wall tucks into a creekbed and is hard to spot until you stand above it. It can bake in summer before shade arrives, so spring and fall are the comfortable seasons. Expect a ridge walk of around twenty minutes or more from the main lot, and likely few other parties.

ca_are_you_experienced_boulder.blurb: A single chalky boulder right at Stinson Beach on the Marin coast, just southwest of the Old Man boulder, with about ten problems. This is a hard-leaning spot: a few moderate lines in the V3 to V5 range, then a steady run of V6 to V8 sits and traverses, with one V10 and one V11 at the top end. Problems are described as burly and crimpy, with slopey holds, and some feel desperate. It gets sun for most of the day apart from the morning, so it can run hot. Topping out means a short downclimb or a step across to the hillside, and it is worth scouting the descent before the first try.

ca_southern_cross.blurb: A buttress north-northeast of May Lake in the Tuolumne Meadows part of Yosemite, up near 10,000 feet. Ten trad routes, mostly alpine in feel, with the best-known ones running about three pitches. Grades go from 5.4 on the easiest line up to 5.9, with the classics in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, and a couple of shorter two-pitch lines around 5.5. The granite is orange, featured and sunny, with plenty of wide cracks, chicken heads and plates, so bring a standard alpine rack plus long slings. It is a good high-country day for a competent party that likes moderate multi-pitch, though the walk up from the May Lake trailhead is a real effort.

ca_potwisha_campground_boulders.blurb: A small bouldering spot beside the river near Potwisha Campground, a few miles inside Sequoia National Park's Highway 198 entrance at about 2,000 feet. Ten problems, nearly all at the gentle end: mostly V0, with a VB, a V2 and a couple of V4s. Expect mild slabs, short cracks and a mantle or two, with one problem flagged as runout. It is not a destination in its own right, but works well for easy warm-ups, a cool-down after Moro Rock, or an afternoon with a few pads and a picnic. The lower elevation makes it one of the park's options outside the high-country summer season.
